documents.title: 1960 Presidential Elections in the Republic of Korea
documents.notes: ROK CIC military-vote plan; police, teachers, village chiefs, arm-band/team/open voting in recent re-elections; Embassy treated them as dress rehearsal indicators.

documents.title: Department telegram 816
documents.notes: U.S. rejected communist-inspired framing as sufficient explanation for Masan unrest and linked unrest to electoral abuses.

documents.title: Eisenhower-Herter telephone conversation
documents.notes: Senior U.S. officials attributed crisis to election conduct and suppression and discussed pressure for free/new election.

documents.title: Department telegram 878
documents.notes: U.S. assessment rejected Rhee framing of Chang Myon/Catholic Church as cause and considered further repression dangerous.

documents.title: Embassy telegram 969
documents.notes: Professor demonstrations; crowd near Yi Ki-pung residence; conflicting reports on shooters; troops generally observed disciplined and avoiding fire.

documents.title: Embassy telegram 986
documents.notes: 09:10 McConaughy urged Defense Minister Kim to press Rhee for student reception, new-election statement, and consideration of political future.

documents.title: Embassy telegram 987
documents.notes: 10:40 Rhee-Kim-Huh-McConaughy meeting; McConaughy urged retirement; Kim appeared to have major drafting/promoting role in four-point program.

documents.title: Editorial Note on Assembly resolution and Rhee resignation
documents.notes: Assembly unanimous resolution; Rhee resignation submission; Huh Chung acting presidency.

documents.title: Department telegram 897
documents.notes: U.S. endorsement of resignation and caretaker transition.

documents.title: Department telegram 949
documents.notes: Huh caretaker government's central unresolved issues: elections, Assembly legitimacy, constitutional revision.
